The Mindbenders - A Groovy Kind Of Love (1965)

This was written by Toni Wine and Carole Bayer Sager and was released first by Diane & Annita in 1965. The song title was an early use of the then-new slang word "groovy". Wine, who was 17 years old when she wrote the song, said, "Carole came up with "Groovy kinda… groovy kinda… groovy…" and we're all just saying, 'Kinda groovy, kinda groovy, kinda…' and I don't exactly know who came up with "Love", but it was 'Groovy kind of love'. And we did it. We wrote it in 20 minutes. It was amazing. Just flew out of our mouths, and at the piano, it was a real quick and easy song to write."

The song was recorded and covered by other bands and artists such as The Turtles and Phil Collins. .

The /v/Museum acquisitions department has again secured another impressive victory. This time, all praise to /u/Some_Guy_from_RI, for finding and providing such a superb addition to the collection.

The painting, also known as "Confidence", shows "...the anecdotal content of a letter containing distressing news." It is one of several paintings by Stevens addressing the theme of consolation.

This might be the interior of a Parisian salon, around the time of the Franco-Prussian war, shortly after the Anglo-Zulu war. (Invention of the telephone and electric light were a couple of years away, in the Gilded Age.)

I immediately loved this painting, first for the beauty of the dresses and the room, and then for the pathos of the scene. I think to us in the 21st Century, with rooms where beauty is often at best a secondary, minor consideration, this is a view of what could be a height of civilization. It seems to be a representation of mankind's attempt for Paradise on Earth.

At the same time, when everything is so near perfection, one dearly wishes nothing to go wrong at all. There is a tension in the painting, the deeply held desire to hold everything together, perhaps until the men return. A sense of proximity to everything about which mankind dreams. Yet there is terrible news.

I have a sense in this picture of a fall from great height, like the Fall of Man from Eden. The poor lady seems to have been cast out of Paradise, and that is the tragedy of the painting.

Hope is represented by the beauty of the lantern.
